item: key files: every name change is flushed to its folder, the freed bytes overwritten, and a wrap in flight can no longer undo an erase
summary: OPEN_QUEUE 2026-10-27 list item 41(c), verified on main 3429b18a before the fix. BEFORE: keyfile.replace_in_place and create_new flushed the key's bytes but never the keys folder, so a power cut right after a plaintext key was wrapped in place could bring the PLAINTEXT file's name back (and the removed plaintext alias back in keys/.pending), on exactly the switched-off machine the at-rest encryption is for; the freed plaintext bytes were only unlinked; and the check that the file was still the one read and the os.replace that acted on it were two steps that quick_crypto_erase, which took no lock, could fall between, so a wrap in flight put the destroyed key back (wrapped) after the erase had counted it destroyed, or left a wrapped copy of it in keys/.pending. NOW: file_lock.flush_folder (A-030's folder flush, now public) runs after every rename, link and alias removal of a key file, in both folders of a rename; a flush failure is logged by class and never turns a done replace into a refusal. A wrap overwrites the bytes it frees with zeros through a handle taken before the replace, when nothing else names them (best effort; no promise on an SSD or a copy-on-write filesystem; skipped on Windows). One process-level lock, keyfile.KEY_FILES_LOCK, is held from the private copy to the folder flush in create_new and replace_in_place (only the key derivation runs outside it), around the restore's take-back of a key it placed (now flushed too), and by the erase from its key step until the whole keys folder (the evidence key and any private copy included) is overwritten and removed, then released before the rest of step 6, so a signing request does not wait on a long data-folder rewrite. A wrap that waited finds its file gone and writes nothing; a creation that waited finds no folder. Stated limits: another process on the same data folder is not covered by the lock; a restore running during an erase can create keys/ again and place the backup's keys, which may be this install's own (serialising restore against erase is not done here); the empty keys/.pending folder's creation and removal are not flushed. Reads: one Opus read and two independent security reads on the first head; their should-fix items (write under the lock, flush inside it, the restore take-back, the test lock release, the erase's long hold) are folded. tests/test_key_file_durability.py: 8 tests, all red on the old code (two of them only for want of the new names); tests/test_evidence_key_wrap.py's interleaving test now pins that the interleaving cannot happen. Release-notes line: «Encryption keys are now flushed to disk whenever they are created or re-wrapped, the unencrypted bytes a re-wrap replaces are overwritten, and an emergency erase can no longer be undone by a key re-wrap running at the same moment.»
